userStories.title: Record and disclose the files the finish-approval advisor opened
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry the advisor's self-reported inspectedFiles through validated replies, decisions and approval outcomes, nudge finish-approval to read code, and disclose the count only in a promoted workflow PR's Summary.

**Motivation** — A PR promoted that way looks the same as one the advisor checked, and nothing in the PR says which it was.

**Approach** — Integration targets from the design (baseline listings locate the code; the targets are the interface to implement):

- `AdvisorReply` (`packages/nax/src/advisor/types.ts`).
  - Baseline: `{ optionId, instruction?, reason?, newText?, rationale, confidence, reversible, needsHumanConfirm }`.
  - Target: adds `inspectedFiles?: string[]`.
- `AdviceDecision` (`packages/nax/src/advisor/types.ts`).
  - Target: adds `inspectedFiles?: string[]`, copied from the reply. Absent when the reply had none.
- `validateAdvisorReply(value, options)` (`packages/nax/src/operations/advise.ts`). Signature unchanged.
  - Baseline: builds the reply from `optionId`, `rationale`, `confidence`, `reversible`, `needsHumanConfirm` and the optional texts.
  - Target: the list is read by a new file-local helper `inspectedFilesOf(raw)` in `advise.ts`, so `validateAdvisorReply` stays under the `check:complexity` limit. When `raw.inspectedFiles` is an array, the reply carries `inspectedFiles` = its string entries whose trimmed text is non-empty, in order (an empty array stays `[]`). When the key is absent or not an array, the reply has no `inspectedFiles` key. The list never makes a reply invalid.
- `decisionDraftFor(...)` (`packages/nax/src/advisor/service-helpers.ts`). Signature unchanged.
  - Target: the drafted decision carries `inspectedFiles` when the reply has it (conditional spread, like `anchorFile`).
- `ApprovalOutcome` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts`).
  - Target: adds `readonly inspectedFiles?: readonly string[]`.
- `askApproval(advisor, input)` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/approval.ts`). Signature unchanged.
  - Target: the approve and hold outcomes carry the decision's `inspectedFiles` when the decision has it; otherwise they are exactly as today.
- `WorkflowPrBodyInput` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/pr-body.ts`).
  - Target: adds `readonly advisorFilesRead?: number`.
- `summary(input)` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/pr-body.ts`).
  - Baseline: the head line, plus "Not ready because:" and the reasons when there are any.
  - Target: when `input.outcome` is `"ready"` and `input.advisorFilesRead` is defined, a second paragraph follows the head line: `The advisor approved from the evidence alone: it listed no files it opened.` when the count is 0, otherwise `The advisor opened <n> file(s) before approving.`. Otherwise unchanged.
- `finishPr(fc, parts, ci, reasons, approval)` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts`).
  - Target: the final `buildWorkflowPrBody({...})` input gains `...(ready ? { advisorFilesRead: approval?.inspectedFiles?.length ?? 0 } : {})`, so a promoted body carries the count and a draft body carries none. `finalize.ts` is at 598 of its 600-line limit (`check:file-sizes`), so this is one added line inside the existing `buildWorkflowPrBody({...})` call, and nothing else in the file grows.
- `CONTRACT` and `advisorQuestionBlock(q)` (`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/advisor-builder.ts`).
  - Baseline: `CONTRACT`'s JSON example has no `inspectedFiles`; the question block is the same for every kind.
  - Target: the JSON example gains `"inspectedFiles": ["path"]`, followed by the sentence `List every file you opened in "inspectedFiles"; an empty list means you ruled from the evidence alone.`. A new exported constant `FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE` = `Before you approve, open at least the changed file you judge riskiest. Use the changed files and the base commit the evidence names, when it names them. List every file you opened in inspectedFiles.` is appended as the question block's last paragraph when `q.kind === "finish-approval"`, and only then. Two callers ask that kind: the workflow `askApproval` (whose evidence carries the base commit and changed-file list) and the finish flow in `src/finish/advise.ts` (whose evidence does not), which is why the rule says "when it names them" and makes no claim about the PR. `buildAdvisorPrompt` includes the question block on both first and continuation turns, so both carry the rule. Tests import `FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE` from `@/prompts/builders/advisor-builder` (test files may reach internals), so `src/prompts/index.ts` is not changed.

`inspectedFiles` is self-reported, the same model the story and branch reviewers already use. Cross-checking it against the session's tool audit is out of scope. An absent list and an empty list both count as zero in the PR body: either way the advisor named no file it opened.

Failure handling:
| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| The advisor reply has no `inspectedFiles`, or it is not an array | The reply is valid, carries no list, and a promoted PR reads it as zero files opened. |
| `inspectedFiles` holds non-strings or blank strings | Those entries are dropped; the rest are kept in order. |

No other new failure paths.

Read-only integration boundaries from the design:
- `packages/nax/src/advisor/service.ts` — `decide(actx, asked, run, severity)` calls `decisionDraftFor(actx, asked.question, run.out.reply, model, severity)` and appends the draft to the ledger; `Advisor.advise` returns `{ decision, fallbackReason }`. Unchanged.
- `packages/nax/src/advisor/batch.ts` and `packages/nax/src/operations/advise-batch.ts` — both validate replies with `validateAdvisorReply` and draft decisions with `decisionDraftFor`, so a batch reply that carries `inspectedFiles` keeps it. The batch prompt (`advisor-batch-builder.ts`) has its own reply contract and does not ask for the list. Unchanged.
- `packages/nax/src/advisor/ledger.ts` — `parseLines` retains the parsed decision object after checking a string `id` and a well-formed `action`, so a decision line carrying `inspectedFiles` reads back unchanged. Its existing validation is unchanged.
- `packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts` — `prMode` calls `askApproval(input.advisor, { feature, evidence })` and passes the outcome to `finishPr(fc, parts, ci, reasons, approval)`.

**Scope** — In: the eight production files above, existing validator/approval/PR-body/advisor-prompt tests, and two new focused test files. The seam is the existing `prMode` → `askApproval` → `finishPr` → `buildWorkflowPrBody` path, entered at `publish`. Create `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/finalize-advisor-reads.test.ts` for AC 15, 16 and 20; `finalize.test.ts` is at 797 of its 800-line limit and its `wire`, `input` and `advisor` helpers are module-local, so this file defines its own minimal `wire` and an `advisor` stub that takes an `inspectedFiles` argument and passes it to `makeAdviceDecision` (the precedent is `finalize-evidence.test.ts`, which carries its own `wire`). Create `packages/nax/test/unit/advisor/service-helpers.test.ts` for AC 6-7; no test file covers `service-helpers.ts` today. Extend `test/unit/operations/advise.test.ts` for AC 1-5, `test/unit/workflow/approval.test.ts` for AC 8, 9, 21, `test/unit/workflow/pr-body.test.ts` for AC 10-13, and `test/unit/prompts/advisor-builder.test.ts` for AC 14, 17-19. Existing no-list assertions and exact outcome pins remain unchanged. Restore injected dependencies after seam tests and assert the last `openOrPromotePr` call, not just the initial draft body.
Out: US-002 owns the shared checklist and state-loss severity text. The finish-approval outcome does not depend on `inspectedFiles`: an approval with zero files opened still promotes the PR, by maintainer ruling 2026-10-18. `inspectedFiles` is not cross-checked against the advisor session's tool audit; the list is taken as reported. A draft PR's body, the `nax workflow status` open items and the decisions sidecar do not show the advisor's file count, and no count field is added to `result.json`; the persisted approval outcome (`FeatureRecord.approval`) carries the `inspectedFiles` list as is. Advisor kinds other than finish-approval get the `inspectedFiles` reply field but no reading rule, and no caller acts on their list. The finish flow's finish-approval question (`src/finish/advise.ts`) receives the reading rule through the shared question block, but its PR body (built by `buildAdvisorSection`) gains no file-count sentence. The batch advisor prompt (`advisor-batch-builder.ts`) does not ask for `inspectedFiles`. US-001 only: a decision line already in a ledger, written before this change, is not rewritten; it reads back with no `inspectedFiles`.

**Interface** — Add `inspectedFiles?: string[]` to `AdvisorReply` and `AdviceDecision`, `readonly inspectedFiles?: readonly string[]` to `ApprovalOutcome`, and `readonly advisorFilesRead?: number` to `WorkflowPrBodyInput`. Preserve the existing signatures of `validateAdvisorReply(value, options)`, `decisionDraftFor(...)`, `askApproval(advisor, input)`, `summary(input)`, and `finishPr(fc, parts, ci, reasons, approval)`. The new file-local helper is `inspectedFilesOf(raw)`. The new exported prompt constant is `FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE` with the exact text above; no prompts barrel export is added.

[unit] validateAdvisorReply given a valid approve reply with no inspectedFiles key returns ok: true and a reply that has no inspectedFiles key.

[unit] buildAdvisorPrompt for a non-continuation question of kind finish-approval returns a prompt containing FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE, and FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE equals Before you approve, open at least the changed file you judge riskiest. Use the changed files and the base commit the evidence names, when it names them. List every file you opened in inspectedFiles.

[unit] publish in pr mode with green gates and CI, with an advisor whose advise returns an approve decision with inspectedFiles: ["src/a.ts", "src/b.ts"], promotes the PR with a body containing The advisor opened 2 file(s) before approving.
[unit] buildAdvisorPrompt with continuation: true for a question of kind finish-approval returns a prompt containing FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE.
[unit] buildAdvisorPrompt for a non-continuation question of kind finish-judgment returns a prompt that omits FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE: the reading rule is added for the finish-approval kind only.

[unit] buildAdvisorPrompt for a question of any kind returns a prompt containing "inspectedFiles" and the sentence List every file you opened in "inspectedFiles"; an empty list means you ruled from the evidence alone.

[unit] publish in pr mode with green gates and CI, with an advisor whose advise returns an approve decision that has no inspectedFiles key, promotes the PR with a body containing The advisor approved from the evidence alone: it listed no files it opened.

[unit] askApproval with an advisor whose advise returns a hold decision with id D-2, rationale risky and inspectedFiles: ["src/a.ts"] returns { approved: false, rationale: "advisor held: risky", decisionId: "D-2", inspectedFiles: ["src/a.ts"] }.

routing.reasoning: Eight small additive production edits reuse existing optional-field spreads, shared validation, prompt composition and the already-wired publish seam; no new integration boundary, abstraction, dependency or security-sensitive behavior is introduced, so focused failing unit and publish-seam tests followed by implementation in one session are sufficient.

userStories.title: Name state loss in the shared workflow review checklist
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a ninth State loss class and a closing reachable-state-loss severity rule to the shared checklist embedded by both workflow reviewers.

**Motivation** — None names a write that replaces a whole entry and so drops fields another writer set.

**Approach** — `WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST` (`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-quality-checklist.ts`).
- Baseline: a heading, one instruction line and eight class bullets, ending with the Reachability bullet.
- Target: exactly this text (the State loss bullet sits after Concurrency and atomicity, and the severity line is last):

```text
## Code-quality checklist
Judge the changed code against each class. Report only what you can quote from a file.
- Concurrency and atomicity: a check and the write it guards in separate statements or transactions; two writers racing on one row, slot or counter; shared mutable state without synchronisation.
- State loss: a write that replaces a whole record, map entry or file that other code also fills, so the fields this write did not set are dropped; a reset, retry or migration that discards state still in use.
- Data-store semantics: the collation or case-sensitivity of identity and unique columns; uniqueness enforced only in code, not by the store; transaction boundaries; column types and widths against the values written.
- Production wiring: an in-memory, fake or test stand-in on a production path where the project provides a shared implementation (an id or sequence generator, cache, lock, queue, storage).
- Test isolation: a test that depends on state another test created; ordering dependence; shared mutable fixtures; globals, environment or files not restored.
- Input safety: untrusted keys used for object lookup (inherited keys such as __proto__ or constructor); unbounded lengths or sizes reaching storage; unvalidated input reaching a query, path or command.
- Performance: a database or network call per item inside a loop on a batch path; serial awaits that could be one batched call.
- Error handling: a swallowed failure; a result or exit code never checked; a default substituted on error so the caller cannot tell empty from broken.
- Reachability: a list with no way past its first page; a state a user or caller cannot reach or leave.
A state loss a caller can reach is a critical or important finding, never minor; if you cannot quote it, put it in cannotVerify.
```

The file's header comment, which says "The eight classes", is updated to nine.

Read-only integration: `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-story-review-builder.ts` (`buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt`) and `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts` (`buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt`) — both embed `WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST` verbatim. Unchanged.

**Scope** — In: `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-quality-checklist.ts` — `WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST` becomes the nine-class text with the closing severity line, and the header comment's "The eight classes" becomes "The nine classes". `packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/workflow-quality-checklist.test.ts` — the test "is the checklist text verbatim (AC-1)" pins the old eight-class `CHECKLIST` literal with `toBe`; the literal becomes the nine-class text with the closing severity line, exactly as the Design target states. The embed tests (AC-3, AC-4) are unchanged. Add focused prompt assertions as needed to prove this story's State loss line in the story prompt and closing severity line in the branch prompt through the existing verbatim embed, not by changing the builders. There are no new files. Include a negative-path prompt test with `concerns: ["Possible state loss without a quotable excerpt"]`, asserting that the returned story prompt still directs unquotable state loss to `cannotVerify` through the exact closing checklist line. This tests emitted guidance, not an actual model's classification. The full exact-text pin also protects all eight pre-existing class bullets against unintended edits.
Out: US-001 owns advisor reply/decision fields, approval propagation, advisor prompt reading instructions and promoted-PR read disclosures. The quality floor (`withQualityFloor` in `workflow/feature-machine.ts`) and the story-review spec rubric are unchanged. The story and branch review reply schemas are unchanged; the severity rule lives only in the shared checklist text.

**Interface** — The existing exported `WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST` remains a shared text constant, not a builder. `buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt` and `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt` retain their current interfaces and verbatim interpolation. Leave `WORKFLOW_ENUMERATION_INSTRUCTION` unchanged. The checklist text above is the exact output contract, including bullet ordering and the final severity line; it is guidance to the reviewers, not a new severity-reclassification algorithm.

analysis:
This is an additive enhancement to the existing TypeScript/Bun workflow and advisor implementation, entirely scoped to packages/nax. The two binding stories are independent, have no dependencies, and must remain separate for independent review and landing. Codebase-memory MCP was unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct reads and text searches. Architecture guidance is indexed at docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:15 (file structure and injectable dependencies), docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:25 (function design and testing), and docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:109 (workflow/advisor subsystems). No implementation or tests were executed while drafting this PRD.

US-001 existing architecture and changes: packages/nax/src/advisor/types.ts:76 defines AdvisorReply and packages/nax/src/advisor/types.ts:88 defines AdviceDecision; both currently lack inspectedFiles. Add optional inspectedFiles?: string[] to each without changing required fields. packages/nax/src/operations/advise.ts:53 defines validateAdvisorReply; its validated object and conditional optional-text fields are assembled at packages/nax/src/operations/advise.ts:74. Add file-local inspectedFilesOf(raw) to filter array entries to strings with non-empty trimmed text while retaining the original string entries and order. Trimming is a predicate, not a normalization requirement: do not deduplicate, sort, canonicalize paths, or change retained string contents. Empty arrays must survive and absent/non-array values must produce no property, never a new invalid-reply path. Extracting this logic preserves the validator's complexity budget. The operation already supplies Read/Glob/Grep at packages/nax/src/operations/advise.ts:101; no new tools or permission/session behavior is needed. packages/nax/src/advisor/service-helpers.ts:67 defines decisionDraftFor and packages/nax/src/advisor/service-helpers.ts:83 demonstrates the conditional-spread convention for optional anchorFile; use the same convention for the reply's list. packages/nax/src/advisor/service.ts:203 already drafts decisions through this helper, so service.ts needs no changes. packages/nax/src/advisor/batch.ts:109 validates replies and packages/nax/src/advisor/batch.ts:118 drafts decisions through the same helper; packages/nax/src/operations/advise-batch.ts:71 also calls the validator. These consumers inherit optional-list preservation without changes or a batch prompt change. packages/nax/src/advisor/ledger.ts:49 parses JSONL decisions and packages/nax/src/advisor/ledger.ts:57 retains the original parsed object after checking its id and well-formed action. It will preserve new fields and read old decisions unchanged; no ledger rewrite or migration is needed.

Workflow seam: packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts:180 defines ApprovalOutcome, and packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts:275 persists it on WorkflowFeatureRecord.approval. Add readonly inspectedFiles?: readonly string[] to ApprovalOutcome. packages/nax/src/workflow/approval.ts:136 defines askApproval; packages/nax/src/workflow/approval.ts:158-160 returns approve/hold outcomes with the decision id. Both branches must conditionally forward inspectedFiles, including [], while outcomes for omitted lists remain exactly equal to existing objects. Leave unavailable/throw fallbacks alone. packages/nax/src/workflow/pr-body.ts:35 defines WorkflowPrBodyInput; add readonly advisorFilesRead?: number. Its summary function at packages/nax/src/workflow/pr-body.ts:56 currently emits the head and optional readiness reasons; add the exact disclosure paragraph only for ready plus a defined count, preserving all other sections, redaction, truncation, and draft behavior. packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:317 defines finishPr, packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:324 derives readiness solely from approval.approved, and packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:326 builds the final body. Add exactly one line to that existing object: ...(ready ? { advisorFilesRead: approval?.inspectedFiles?.length ?? 0 } : {}). The file currently has 598 lines against the spec's 600-line limit, so do not grow anything else there or refactor unrelated publish logic. packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:543 calls askApproval with approval evidence, and packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:557 forwards the outcome to finishPr. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:490 already passes out.approval into persisted feature state; no separate result.json count or persistence patch is required. packages/nax/src/workflow/open-items.ts:51 consumes the approval for open items and must not gain count presentation. This is disclosure, not enforcement: approved empty/omitted lists still promote. Counts are list lengths, not audit-verified or unique-file counts.

Advisor prompts: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/advisor-builder.ts:41 defines advisorQuestionBlock and packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/advisor-builder.ts:52 defines CONTRACT. Extend the common JSON contract and add the exact explanatory sentence for every kind. Export FINISH_APPROVAL_READ_RULE from this builder only, append it as the question block's last paragraph only for finish-approval, and leave src/prompts/index.ts unchanged. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/advisor-builder.ts:60 builds prompts and includes the question block and contract on both first and continuation turns. The same kind is also asked at packages/nax/src/finish/advise.ts:191, so that flow gets the shared reading rule without any finish PR-body change. The existing policy at packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/advisor-builder.ts:24 remains untouched; do not turn any prompt instruction into a new deterministic hold. The rule's conditional wording about evidence accommodates the two callers.

US-001 test plan and constraints: packages/nax/test/unit/operations/advise.test.ts:35 covers validator behavior and packages/nax/test/unit/operations/advise.test.ts:88 covers the operation.
